name: חָנָן
summary: The root's verb or adjective standing alone, perhaps a short form of names such as אֶלְחָנָן and יוֹחָנָן. Borne by one of David's mighty men, son of Maacah (1Ch 11:43); two Benjamites (1Ch 8:23, 38; 9:44); Hanan son of Igdaliah, “the man of God”, whose sons had a chamber in the house of Yahweh (Jer 35:4); the head of a family of Nethinim (Ezr 2:46; Neh 7:49); a Levite who helped the people understand the law and sealed the covenant (Neh 8:7; 10:11); two chiefs who sealed it (Neh 10:23, 27); and Hanan son of Zaccur, made a treasurer “for they were counted faithful” (Neh 13:13).

evidence.note: “חָנָן son of Maacah”, among David's mighty men.
“The chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God.”
Among the Levites who “caused the people to understand the law”.
“Hanan son of Zaccur … for they were counted faithful.”
The verb: “the children whom God has graciously given (חָנַן) your servant”.

note: Takes h.dz.ag. The database also files under it, by spelling, the חָנָן of בַּעַל חָנָן (Gen 36:38–39; 1Ch 1:49–50; 1Ch 27:28), of בֶּן־חָנָן (1Ch 4:20), and of the place אֵילוֹן בֵּית חָנָן (1Ki 4:9); the first two are tagged in baal-hanan and ben-hanan by their own keys. TIPNR's Neh.10.22 and Neh.10.26 are Neh 10:23 and 10:27 in the Hebrew numbering; TIPNR counts the Levite of Neh 10:11 with Hanan@Neh.8.7. Whether the name is the verb (“he has been gracious”, with God understood) or an adjective (“gracious”) the form does not decide.
